newsitem.title: USA: R.R. Donnelley feels restructuring impact.
newsitem.headline: R.R. Donnelley feels restructuring impact.

text.p: R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co, posting weaker operating results for the 1996 fourth quarter and full year, said results were affected by restructuring charges of $435 million after-tax.

The charges were mainly to realign its gravure printing operations in North America and to reposition its software production, distribution and support businesses. They were partly offset by pre-tax gains on the initial public offerings of Donnelley Enterprise Solutions Inc in the fourth quarter and Metromail Corp in the second quarter.

Donnelley said operating earnings from print-related businesses in the fourth quarter declined 10 percent from a year ago to $142 million. For the full year, excluding restructuring charges, operating earnings were $454 million, down 14 percent from 1995.

The company said software-related businesses reported an operating loss of $10 million in the quarter and, excluding restructuring charges, $29 million for the full year. These results compare with operating earnings of $17 million in the 1995 fourth quarter and $32 million for all of 1995.

"We took direct and decisive action in 1996 to strengthen our strategic focus, improve productivity and asset utilization and reduce costs," said acting chairman John Richman in a statement. He said paper-price volatility that affected results in recent years "seems unlikely to recur to the same degree in the near future."

Earlier, Donnelley posted fourth-quarter net earnings per share of $0.66, or $0.51, before restructuring charges and a full-year loss of $1.04 a share, or a profit of $1.51 before restructuring charges.
